E1.label: Thermal / Sensor Error
E1.diagnosis: Possible temperature sensor failure (open circuit) or abnormal overheating.
E1.solution: Unplug the air fryer and let it cool for 15-60 minutes. If the error persists, contact customer support.

E2.label: Sensor Short Circuit
E2.diagnosis: Short circuit in the temperature sensor, or (on some dual-basket models) missing divider.
E2.solution: Unplug and contact support. If the model requires a divider, ensure it is installed correctly.

E3.label: Overheat Protection
E3.diagnosis: The overheat protection system has activated.
E3.solution: Immediately unplug the appliance and let it cool completely before using it again.

E4.label: Power or Malfunction
E4.diagnosis: Incorrect power voltage or generic device malfunction.
E4.solution: Unplug and replug into the outlet. Verify the correct voltage. If it persists, contact support.

Display Spento.label: No Power
Display Spento.diagnosis: The device is not receiving electrical power.
Display Spento.solution: Check that the plug is inserted, verify the fuse or try a different outlet.

E1.label: Faulty / Cold Device
E1.diagnosis: The device is broken/defective or was stored in a very cold place.
E1.solution: Let it warm at room temperature for at least 15-60 minutes before plugging it in. If it persists, contact Philips support.

E2.label: Missing Divider
E2.diagnosis: The divider is not installed and small basket cooking was attempted.
E2.solution: Install the divider. Let it cool for 2 minutes and reinsert.

E1.label: Error
E1.diagnosis: There is an open circuit in the temperature monitor. Contact Customer Support

E2.label: Error
E2.diagnosis: There is a short circuit in the temperature monitor. Contact Customer Support

E3.label: Error
E3.diagnosis: The air fryer's overheat protection has activated. Turn off and unplug the air fryer and allow it to cool completely. If the display continues to show "E3", contact Customer Support

E4.label: Error
E4.diagnosis: The air fryer has been plugged into a 220–240V outlet. Turn off and unplug the air fryer. Only use the air fryer with 120V, 60Hz outlets
